findings.source_passage: This was strangely heightened at times by the ragged Elijah's diabolical incoherences uninvitedly recurring to me, with a subtle energy I could not have before conceived of. But poorly could I withstand them, much as in other moods I was almost ready to smile at the solemn whimsicalities of that outlandish prophet of the wharves.
findings.why_it_matters: Ishmael's voice-defining self-analysis—his ambivalence between dismissal and dread, the phrase 'outlandish prophet of the wharves'—is collapsed to a bare clause. This sustained ironic interiority is what distinguishes Ishmael's narration; flattening it erases the narrator's consciousness.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at minimum 'much as in other moods I was almost ready to smile at the solemn whimsicalities of that outlandish prophet of the wharves' to preserve Ishmael's characteristic double-register.

findings.source_passage: they were every one of them Americans; a Nantucketer, a Vineyarder, a Cape man
findings.why_it_matters: The terse catalog 'a Nantucketer, a Vineyarder, a Cape man' is a rhythmically and culturally distinctive passage; it characterizes the mates in the book's economic, regional shorthand and contributes to the thematic Americanness of the crew. It is entirely absent.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the list within the mention of the mates allaying misgivings: 'three Americans—a Nantucketer, a Vineyarder, a Cape man.'

findings.source_passage: not a little of this overbearing grimness was owing to the barbaric white leg upon which he partly stood
findings.source_locator: Fifth paragraph, the sentence introducing the ivory leg
findings.why_it_matters: The source records that the narrating consciousness was so overwhelmed by Ahab's total aspect that the ivory leg was initially overlooked—a significant interpretive moment showing how Ahab's presence overshadows even his most famous physical feature. The draft skips directly to the leg without this framing.
findings.suggested_fix: Include the 'so powerfully did the whole grim aspect affect me' sentence noting that the ivory leg registered only secondarily, before describing it.

findings.source_passage: the clouds that layer upon layer were piled upon his brow, as ever all clouds choose the loftiest peaks to pile themselves upon
findings.why_it_matters: The extended simile—'as ever all clouds choose the loftiest peaks to pile themselves upon'—is a small but characteristic piece of Melville's cosmological metaphorizing that the draft strips to 'the clouds piled upon his brow.'
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the tail clause to keep the cosmic register: 'the clouds that layer upon layer were piled upon his brow, as ever all clouds choose the loftiest peaks.'

summary: The draft is broadly faithful and preserves the most famous signatures (bronze/Perseus, lightning-scar simile, crucifixion in his face, the April-and-May oak finale), but flattens Ishmael's ironic voice-interiority in the second paragraph, drops the culturally resonant mates-catalog, and elides the narratively significant moment of the ivory leg being registered only belatedly—three medium findings that approach but do not cross the regeneration threshold.
